newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL FIPE DEFLATION AT 0.28 PCT - FIPE.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL FIPE DEFLATION AT 0.28 PCT - FIPE.

text.p: Brazil's deflation as measured by the Economic Research Institute (Fipe) was 0.28 percent between July 8 and August 7, down from 0.11 percent inflation in the previous four-week period, a Fipe official said.
Fipe chief Juarez Rizzieri said it was the first time "for a long time" that the Fipe index recorded deflation rather than inflation in prices.
He said lower food prices, especially fruit and cereals, and end of season clothing sales contributed to a slowing in the price index, which measures costs in the city of Sao Paulo.
Rizzieri said he expected the month of August to close with deflation of 0.5 percent, and even if there were inflation it would be only slight.
He gave the following breakdown of the Fipe weighted index for the period (rise unless indicated).
The Fipe index is calculated by the University of Sao Paulo, which releases inflation figures at weekly intervals.
